Uganda based participants representing Ugandan civil society and WROs attended a number of critical cross movement spaces including 2024 Feminist Leadership Movement Building and Rights Institute (FLMBaRI) led by CREA which took place in Kampala, DSROI EA (virtual); CoSP (virtual); a pre-GSWF regional conference in Kenya, a digital security training in Kenya and AWID in Bangkok. Through engaging with WGG, two Uganda based organizations and actors, specifically Femme Forte and Diverse Empowerment represented their organizations and strong WGG politics to forge meaningful alliances with other structurally excluded groups.

20 - 1) CREA’s Feminist leadership, Movement Building, and Rights Institute, FLMBRI – East Africa is a residential program designed to strengthen feminist solidarity, leadership, advocacy, and strategies for building collective power for social transformation. The Institute engages feminists from across the region to build a substantive understanding of our present with all its challenges and possibilities. It interrogates concepts and structures that affect our strategies by embedding patriarchy and gender in concepts of nation, identity, religion, polity, and development. To make meaning of what feminist struggles have transformed and how new forms of patriarchy are part of existing inequalities. 7 participatns from Ugandan CSOs attended the 2023 FLMBRI. 2) The Movement Strengthening Initiative (MSI) is a pioneering initiative which was piloted under CREA leadership and supported through Women Gaining Ground (WGG) program. It aims to build cross-movement alliances by intentionally connecting movement actors across national borders and intersecting movements in East Africa. With this initial session we focused on bringing together the Feminist movement, the Disability Justice movement, the Sex worker movement, and the LBTQI+ movements. It was also intended to deepen awareness of issues related to Women with Disabilities (WWD) and young (trans-inclusive) women in the thematic area of Sexual and Gender-Based Violence. There were 9 Uganda participants fromsacross CSOs and various movements who participated in it.(3) DSROI – East Africa brought together a total of twenty three participants (Feminists, women rights activists and disability rights activists) drawn from Women Gaining Ground (WGG) East Africa - Kenya, Uganda and Rwanda. There were 4 participants from Uganda including from feminist and disability rights organizations. The objective of the Institute was to strengthen critical understanding of the intersections of disability, gender and sexuality amongst feminists, disability rights, women rights activists and provide an analytical framework to address the intersectional and multiple forms of discrimination they experience as well as fostering cross movement collaboration.

Women's rights networks and alliances engage to create actions to have a diverse representation of GWWDs

On August 24th, 2022, CREA's partner, hosted a meeting to promote disability inclusion. As a result, 11 organizations known as WROs and 25 individuals gained knowledge about how to include girls and women with disabilities (WGWDs) in their activities. The WROs now have an understanding of the reasonable accommodation needs for each category of disability and have included the associated costs in their budgets. This newfound awareness came about because the meeting introduced the challenges faced by WGWDs and how WROs can assist them.
